Subject: Private endpoint egress containment — evidence request

Ben —

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. As part of our security sign-off we need:

- A concise, machine-parsable list of all outbound egress destinations (IP ranges and FQDNs) that Redwood's private endpoint will talk to from our VPC during normal operation and during model fallbacks.
- Any TLS SNI hostnames you rely on (if SNI-based firewalling is required).
- Whether Redwood requires outbound HTTP(S) to arbitrary third-party domains (CDNs, telemetry) or whether those are pinned to explicit hostnames.
- Rotating/ephemeral IP behavior and the cadence of rotations (if applicable).
- A short verification plan we can execute from our perimeter (curl/wget checks, expected headers, and a minimal payload) so we can confirm containment without sharing credentials.
- A short list of evidence artifacts you can provide (pcap, egress logs, signed statement) and an estimated delivery date.

We need to get this into our SOC-2 evidence folder by Friday 2027-07-23. Can you confirm what you can provide and by when?

Thanks —
Grace

Grace —

Appreciate the list — we can provide the items you requested. High level: Redwood Private (control plane + runtime) will not reach out to arbitrary third parties from customer private endpoints. Outbound traffic from the private runtime is limited to:

- Redwood-managed control plane endpoints (hostnames and IP ranges provided below).
- Optional telemetry/metrics endpoints (customer opt-in; otherwise disabled).
- Model store artifacts when using Redwood-hosted models (pinned FQDNs).

I'll loop in Laura (runtime/networking) for the exact CIDR blocks and the verification artifacts. Marissa will align on timelines for SOC-2 packaging.

Planned deliverables by EOD 2027-07-23:
- CSV of allowed outbound IPs and FQDNs (egress-allowlist-20270722.csv)
- A signed statement of containment and IP rotation cadence (in meridian-egress-evidence.zip)
- A one-page verification runbook with sample curl commands (egress-verification-runbook.pdf)

If you need anything earlier, tell us which artifact is highest priority and we’ll push it.

Best,

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private endpoint egress containment — evidence request

Grace —

Attached is the CSV with the allowlist we maintain for private endpoints. Summary (technical):

- Primary outbound: TLS 443 to the following hostnames (SNI required for host-based firewalls):
  - ctl.redwood-inference.com -> 34.216.12.0/24, 34.216.13.0/24
  - artifacts.redwood-inference.com -> 52.11.44.0/24 (model fetch only)

- Fallback/compat: in constrained capacity, Redwood may failover to regional-compatible endpoints under the same hostnames; IPs are within the ranges above.

- DNS requirements: customer environment must allow resolution of the above FQDNs. We do not rely on arbitrary external CDNs for model fetch once the model is pinned.

- Egress proxy support: Customers may route runtime egress through a customer-managed outbound proxy. In that case we require mutual TLS (client cert) from the runtime to the proxy and expect the proxy to forward TLS to Redwood endpoint without TLS termination (SNI passthrough preferred).

- Rotation: IP rotation window is scheduled monthly for artifacts endpoints; control plane ranges change only on major infra updates (we will provide 30-day notice and a pinned fallback range for emergency).

Evidence package contents (in meridian-egress-evidence.zip):
- signed-containment-statement.txt (GPG-signed by Redwood infra lead)
- pcap-sample-20270722.pcap (3 minute capture from a lab private endpoint hitting ctl.redwood-inference.com)
- egress-allowlist-20270722.csv
- egress-verification-runbook.pdf

Sample verification steps (high-level):
1) From a bastion in your VPC, run: 
   curl -v --resolve \"ctl.redwood-inference.com:443:34.216.12.5\" https://ctl.redwood-inference.com/healthz --header \"x-rw-check: meridian-test\"
   Expected: 200 OK, header x-rw-check: accepted
2) DNS-only check: nslookup ctl.redwood-inference.com -> should resolve to listed IPs.
3) TLS SNI check: s_client -servername ctl.redwood-inference.com -connect 34.216.12.5:443 and verify certificate CN/SAN.

If you want a short-lived support window we can run a live canary test from our side while you observe.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Network & Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

3) Health endpoint (no auth, test header): 
   curl -v --resolve \"ctl.redwood-inference.com:443:34.216.12.5\" https://ctl.redwood-inference.com/healthz 
   Expected: 200 OK and header x-rw-check: accepted
